title: AI exposure can intensify displacement fear unless management makes worker value and transition visible
source_unit: Gallup Workplace, Using AI More Does Not Reassure Workers, Managers Do, September 9, 2026
geography: United States; employed adults aged 18 and older in Gallup Panel workforce studies

denominator.unit: nearly 30,000 unique worker observations across four Gallup Panel workforce-study waves; approximately 30% observed in two or more waves

frequent_user_displacement_pattern.value: Workers using AI daily or multiple times a week report more than twice the acute displacement concern of workers using AI a few times a month or year in most survey waves.

all_worker_somewhat_or_very_likely.unit: percent saying their job is somewhat or very likely to be eliminated by AI as of Q1 2026

acute_concern_pattern.value: Across most waves, roughly 3%-4% report that job elimination within five years due to new technology, automation or AI is very likely, with materially higher rates among frequent AI users.

observations.method: Gallup pooled analysis of four nationally representative Gallup Panel workforce-study waves from 2023 through the first quarter of 2026; employed adults aged 18 and older, weighted to the U.S. adult population.
observations.uncertainty: The study is observational even where it follows the same workers; frequent AI use may reflect occupation, task exposure, organizational change or worker selection, and the article does not present a randomized exposure design.
observations.subgroup: Frequent AI users versus workers using AI only a few times a month or year; comparisons account for broad occupation, industry and demographic differences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Frequent users may perceive real task substitution earlier because they are closer to the technology, not because use itself causes anxiety; nonusers may be less informed about their exposure.

observations.period: 2023 through Q1 2026; management support as a buffer

denominator.unit: nearly 30,000 unique worker observations in the pooled panel analysis

respect_buffer.unit: percentage-point smaller association between frequent AI use and displacement fear among workers giving the highest respect rating versus lower ratings

wellbeing_care_buffer.unit: percentage-point smaller association among workers who feel their organization cares about their wellbeing

management_mechanism.value: Manager communication about the purpose of AI, worker value, changing skills and evaluation appears to moderate how workers interpret the same technology exposure.
management_mechanism.unit: analytical synthesis grounded in reported associations

observations.method: Gallup comparison of AI-use and displacement-fear associations by organizational respect and perceived care for employee wellbeing, including within-worker tracking and controls for time trends across industry and occupation.
observations.uncertainty: The reported buffers are associations and do not identify which management intervention caused the difference; respect and care may be correlated with job quality, leadership, security, resources and selection into workplaces.
observations.subgroup: Frequent AI users exposed to stronger versus weaker reported management support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Supportive management may reduce fear by improving information and voice, or it may simply identify organizations that are less likely to eliminate jobs and better able to absorb technology.

observations.period: 2023 through Q1 2026; displacement fear and worker outcomes

denominator.unit: nearly 30,000 unique worker observations in the pooled panel analysis

engagement_change.unit: standard deviations in employee engagement when the same worker reported displacement concern versus no such concern

burnout_change.unit: standard deviations higher burnout in the within-worker comparison

job_satisfaction_change.unit: standard deviations lower job satisfaction in the within-worker comparison

active_job_search_change.unit: percentage-point greater likelihood of actively looking for another job

observations.method: Within-worker longitudinal comparisons from repeated Gallup Panel workforce studies, with adjustment for stable worker differences including personality, baseline optimism and job type.
observations.uncertainty: The reported within-worker associations reduce some time-invariant confounding but do not prove that displacement fear caused the outcomes; changing workplace conditions, health, management or broader economic shocks may move together.
observations.subgroup: Workers reporting at least some likelihood of AI-related job elimination versus the same workers reporting no such concern.
observations.counterinterpretation: Engagement, burnout, satisfaction and job-search activity may also change how workers answer questions about job risk, creating reciprocal or common-cause relationships.

boundary: This record adds a worker-level implementation mechanism to the AI transition theme: the same AI exposure can be interpreted as threat or manageable change depending partly on respect, wellbeing support, communication and perceived worker value. The source is observational panel analysis; it does not establish causal effects of AI use or management, actual job elimination, productivity, wages, retention or successful transition.
